label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent many years residing in Brierley.
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent many years residing in Brierley, serving as a pillar of community organizations such as the Sewing Circle, Sunday-school, Church Aid Society, and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. One June afternoon, she observed Obed Abernethy dressed in fine clothes driving toward town, triggering her intense curiosity. After investigating at Grey Shutters, she learned from Thirza Abernethy that they intended to adopt an orphanage boy. When Obed brought home a girl, Nell Harcourt, instead of a boy, Agatha eventually visited Grey Shutters after recovering from a bout of influenza to inspect the orphan. During the visit, Agatha bluntly criticized Nell's appearance, driving the child into a furious temper tantrum. Agatha advised Thirza to discipline Nell with a birch rod, but after Nell later offered a complete and theatrical apology, Agatha fully forgave her and grew fond of her. Later, when Thirza mistakenly accused Nell of losing an amethyst brooch, Agatha took part in punishing and then exonerating the girl. Over the following years, Agatha monitored Nell's progress at school and provided advice and commentary on various village events, including the arrival of the new minister and the Sunday-school picnic. After her husband Thomas passed away, she eventually made plans to sell her farm and move into Grey Shutters with Thirza.

value: Barney brought groups of attendees out rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters.
unit: During the Sunday-school picnic at Brierley, Barney brought groups of attendees out rowing six at a time on the Lake of Glassy Waters. When Odette Pullen nearly fell into the water reaching for lilies, Gorham Pullen caught her by her sash, which Barney later reflected would have made a romantic adventure had it happened to someone else. Later in the summer, Barney was recruited by Thirza Abernethy to harness the sorrel horse to take Nell Harcourt to the picnic. Later that evening, he drove a double-seated buggy containing Nell, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen to the Sunday-school picnic event. During the journey, he demanded that Nell sit beside him on the front seat, taking great pride in driving with her at his side despite his inability to converse easily.

label: History
value: Flossie attends Brierley school.
unit: Flossie attends Brierley school, where she is caught cheating by looking at her book during a spelling class. Later, she mocks Nell Harcourt during class, leading Nell to break a slate over Hugh Carrow's head. At Mr. Pembroke's garden party, Flossie boasts of her fence-walking skills and dares Nell to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof, which results in Nell falling and spraining her ankle. During Nell's recovery, Flossie visits her out of apparent regret. She later joins the Regent's entrance class under Miss Thorne, though she refuses to participate in a school concert dialogue after failing to secure the role of the Fairy Queen. She eventually passes the entrance examination and attends Regent's Academy in Portmaris.

label: History
value: Honora attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Honora attended Regent's Academy, where she became a close friend of Nell Harcourt, Cressida Lindsay, Mabel Colby, and Odette Pullen. After graduating from her initial studies, she enrolled at Wexcombe College alongside Nell to pursue higher education, earning honors in Classics during her Freshman year. During her time at college, she rented and co-managed 'Tabby's Place,' a quaint house on Linden Avenue, alongside Nell, Mabel, Cressida, and her aunt, Jamesina. Honora's aunt, the author Charlotte E. Varley, visited her on Prince Edward Island and in Toronto, providing her with literary inspiration and connections.

During her time at college, she rented and co-managed 'Tabby's Place,' a quaint house on Linden Avenue, alongside Nell, Mabel, Cressida, and her aunt, Jamesina. Honora's aunt, the author Charlotte E. Varley, visited her on Prince Edward Island and in Toronto, providing her with literary inspiration and connections.

label: History
value: Hugh Carrow spends several years out west in Alberta.
unit: After spending several years out west in Alberta due to his father's health, Hugh Carrow returns to Brierley to resume his schooling under Mr. Pidgeon. Upon returning from a summer in New Brunswick, he joins the fourth book class and quickly becomes the top student. He gets into trouble with Nell Harcourt when he pulls her braid and calls her 'Carrots', leading her to break her slate over his head. Though he attempts to apologize, Nell holds a grudge against him. During the term, he is forced to sit beside Nell as a punishment after a group tardiness incident, where he tries to offer her a sweethearts' candy, which she crushes underfoot. Despite Nell's hostility, Hugh competes vigorously with her for academic honors, eventually advancing alongside her to the fifth class and studying advanced branches like Latin and geometry. Later, he performs a recitation of 'Bingen on the Rhine' at the Brierley Debating Club concert, during which he retrieves a rose dropped by Nell. After finishing his studies at Brierley, he resigns his application for the Brierley school so Nell can have the teaching position, accepting a job at Pale Sands instead. He eventually encounters Nell on her way back from the cemetery and begs for her forgiveness, which she grants, leading to a close friendship between them.

value: Isolde gets sick from accidentally drinking homemade currant wine at Grey Shutters.
unit: When Isolde gets sick from accidentally drinking homemade currant wine at Grey Shutters, her strict mother forbids her from playing with Nell. Despite the restriction, Isolde sneaks out to say a tearful farewell to Nell at the Nymph's Well, swearing her eternal love. Later, after Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup, Mrs. Pembroke repents and permits the girls to resume their friendship. During a visit from her strict great-aunt, Miss Lavinia Pembroke, Isolde and Nell accidentally jump onto the bed in the spare room while she is sleeping, but Nell takes the blame and wins Aunt Lavinia over. Isolde later attends Brierley school, where she shares a desk with Nell and navigates school life, teasing from Hugh Carrow, and various social events alongside her closest friend.

value: Nell is pale.

label: Personality
value: Nell is vibrant.

She is deeply appreciative of beauty in nature and poetry, constantly inventing creative names for places and things. Though loquacious and easily carried away by daydreams, she is obedient, soft-hearted, and eager to prove herself dutiful and appreciative to those who care for her.

label: History
value: Nell is brought from a Nova Scotia orphanage to Brierley, Prince Edward Island
unit: Nell is mistakenly brought from a Nova Scotia orphanage to Brierley, Prince Edward Island by Mrs. Alexander Tranter, because Thirza and Obed Abernethy had intended to adopt an eleven-year-old boy to help on their farm. Upon her arrival at Grey Shutters, Thirza initially insists she must be sent back, but Obed is charmed by her loquacious nature, and Thirza eventually agrees to keep her after taking pity on her hard upbringing. Nell adapts eagerly to her new home, forming a deep friendship with her neighbor Isolde Pembroke and naming various landmarks around Brierley. After an outburst of rage against neighbor Agatha Sowerby over comments about her appearance, Nell eventually apologizes and earns Agatha's fondness. Nell attends Sunday school and Brierley school, where she forms a fierce academic rivalry with student Hugh Carrow, who angers her by teasing her about her red hair. Nell mistakenly dyes her hair green with peddler's dye, forcing Thirza to crop it short. When a mix-up over a missing brooch leads Thirza to ban Nell from a Sunday-school picnic, Nell fabricates a dramatic confession, but the brooch is found and she attends after all. During a winter night, Nell successfully saves the life of Isolde's infant sister Posy Fay when she contracts croup, using skills learned caring for twins in her past, which heals a rift with Mrs. Pembroke. After a teacher's punishment prompts Nell to temporarily quit school, she is allowed to study at home, eventually advancing to the fifth class. unit: Nell is mistakenly brought from a Nova Scotia orphanage to Brierley, Prince Edward Island by Mrs. Alexander Tranter, because Thirza and Obed Abernethy had intended to adopt an eleven-year-old boy to help on their farm. Upon her arrival at Grey Shutters, Thirza initially insists she must be sent back, but Obed is charmed by her loquacious nature, and Thirza eventually agrees to keep her after taking pity on her hard upbringing. Nell adapts eagerly to her new home, forming a deep friendship with her neighbor Isolde Pembroke and naming various landmarks around Brierley. After an outburst of rage against neighbor Agatha Sowerby over comments about her appearance, Nell eventually apologizes and earns Agatha's fondness. Nell attends Sunday school and Brierley school, where she forms a fierce academic rivalry with student Hugh Carrow, who angers her by teasing her about her red hair. Nell mistakenly dyes her hair green with peddler's dye, forcing Thirza to crop it short. When a mix-up over a missing brooch leads Thirza to ban Nell from a Sunday-school picnic, Nell fabricates a dramatic confession, but the brooch is found and she attends after all. During a winter night, Nell successfully saves the life of Isolde's infant sister Posy Fay when she contracts croup, using skills learned caring for twins in her past, which heals a rift with Mrs. Pembroke. After a teacher's punishment prompts Nell to temporarily quit school, she is allowed to study at home, eventually advancing to the fifth class. label: History
value: Obed resides at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed resides at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister, Thirza Abernethy. Facing increasing age, heart trouble, and difficulty in securing farm labor, he and Thirza decide to adopt an intelligent, promising orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist on the farm. Obed travels to the Alder River station to collect the boy, only to discover that a misunderstanding led to the arrival of an eleven-year-old girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Being too bashful to break the news to the enthusiastic child, Obed brings her home to Grey Shutters for Thirza to address the mistake. Despite the mix-up, Obed takes an immediate liking to Nell's loquacious chatter during the drive and quietly opposes Thirza's intention to send her back. When Thirza attempts to hand Nell over to the harsh Mrs. Peter Scobie, Obed refuses to let her go to such a home. He continues to advocate for Nell until Thirza agrees to keep her. Later, when Nell is confined to her room for a temperamental outburst against Agatha Sowerby, Obed secretly visits her upstairs and gently persuades her to apologize so she can end her isolation. Throughout Nell's settling at Grey Shutters, Obed remains a sympathetic father figure, occasionally buying her treats like chocolate sweeties.

label: History

unit: Odette Pullen resides in Brierley. Her father, Robert, miscommunicated a message sent by Obed and Thirza Abernethy regarding the adoption of an orphan boy, causing her aunt, Mrs. Alexander Tranter, to bring back a girl instead. When Thirza Abernethy and Nell visited Mrs. Tranter at Pale Sands Cove, Odette helped welcome the guests and prepared tea in the kitchen. Later, she attended a Sunday-school picnic at Lake of Glassy Waters, where she nearly fell into the water while reaching for water lilies before her father caught her.

label: History
value: Opal attends Brierley school
unit: Opal attends Brierley school alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. She becomes known among the pupils for monitoring teacher Mr. Pidgeon's romantic interest in older student Sukey Pullen. During one afternoon class, she collapses back onto her chair with a faint scream and begins weeping when Hugh Carrow secretly attaches her long blonde plait to the back of her seat. On a subsequent occasion when pupils arrive late after gathering spruce gum, she becomes terribly pale with fear and later recounts to her peers how white Nell turned when forced to sit next to Hugh Carrow as a punishment. She also lends an apple to Nell during her first day at school.

label: History
value: Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster
unit: Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster for the Brierley school during Nell Harcourt's first year in the community. His position was secured through his uncle, who was a dominant school trustee. As a teacher, he focused most of his efforts on older pupils preparing for the Regent's Academy exam—particularly Sukey Pullen, with whom he was hopelessly in love—while neglecting the younger children. During class, he frequently sat with Sukey to clarify coursework, wrote messages on her slate, and twirled his mustache. On one occasion, when Nell Harcourt reacted to Hugh Carrow pulling her hair by smashing a slate over Hugh's head, Pidgeon disciplined Nell by forcing her to stand on the dais before the blackboard with a reprimand written above her. Later, after a group of students arrived late to class, Pidgeon singled out Nell and forced her to sit beside Hugh Carrow as a penalty, prompting Nell to temporarily quit attending school. Pidgeon also participated in local community events; at the Sunday-school picnic, he brought attendees out rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters, and at the Brierley Debating Club concert, he delivered Mark Antony's address above Caesar's form. At the end of the school term, he gave a moving farewell speech to his students, which brought many to tears, before departing Brierley.

unit: Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster for the Brierley school during Nell Harcourt's first year in the community. His position was secured through his uncle, who was a dominant school trustee. As a teacher, he focused most of his efforts on older pupils preparing for the Regent's Academy exam—particularly Sukey Pullen, with whom he was hopelessly in love—while neglecting the younger children. During class, he frequently sat with Sukey to clarify coursework, wrote messages on her slate, and twirled his mustache. On one occasion, when Nell Harcourt reacted to Hugh Carrow pulling her hair by smashing a slate over Hugh's head, Pidgeon disciplined Nell by forcing her to stand on the dais before the blackboard with a reprimand written above her. Later, after a group of students arrived late to class, Pidgeon singled out Nell and forced her to sit beside Hugh Carrow as a penalty, prompting Nell to temporarily quit attending school. Pidgeon also participated in local community events; at the Sunday-school picnic, he brought attendees out rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters, and at the Brierley Debating Club concert, he delivered Mark Antony's address above Caesar's form. At the end of the school term, he gave a moving farewell speech to his students, which brought many to tears, before departing Brierley.

label: History
value: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters
unit: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed Abernethy. Expecting an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist on the farm, she is shocked when Obed returns from the train station with an eleven-year-old red-haired girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Though initially determined to send Nell back due to her uselessness on a farm and her loquacious, overly imaginative nature, Thirza develops sympathy for the child's deprived background and agrees to take her in permanently. Thirza takes charge of Nell's upbringing, attempting to curb her excessive imagination, instill religious education, and teach her practical duties like dishwashing, sewing, and bedmaking. When neighbor Agatha Sowerby insults Nell's appearance and triggers a fiery outburst, Thirza punishes Nell by confining her to her room until she apologizes, while surprisingly defending Nell to Agatha. Later, Thirza wrongly accuses Nell of stealing her treasured amethyst brooch; when the brooch is found caught in a shawl, Thirza realizes her mistake and reconciles with Nell. When Nell falls ill from a sprained ankle after walking a roof ridgepole, Thirza realizes how deeply she has come to love her foster daughter. Later, Thirza goes to Port Marlow to hear the Canadian Premier speak, leaving Nell and Obed at home. After Obed dies suddenly from a heart attack caused by the failure of the Abbey Bank, Thirza faces the loss of their life savings and contemplates selling Grey Shutters, but Nell refuses to let the home go and chooses to stay and teach at the Brierley school instead of attending college. Thirza's eyesight deteriorates, requiring a doctor's order to stop reading and sewing, prompting her to invite the widowed Agatha Sowerby to live with her at Grey Shutters so Nell can finally attend Wexcombe College. Years later, Thirza witnesses Nell's graduation with High Honors and her marriage to Hugh Carrow in the orchard of Grey Shutters.

Though initially determined to send Nell back due to her uselessness on a farm and her loquacious, overly imaginative nature, Thirza develops sympathy for the child's deprived background and agrees to take her in permanently. Thirza takes charge of Nell's upbringing, attempting to curb her excessive imagination, instill religious education, and teach her practical duties like dishwashing, sewing, and bedmaking. When neighbor Agatha Sowerby insults Nell's appearance and triggers a fiery outburst, Thirza punishes Nell by confining her to her room until she apologizes, while surprisingly defending Nell to Agatha. Later, Thirza wrongly accuses Nell of stealing her treasured amethyst brooch; when the brooch is found caught in a shawl, Thirza realizes her mistake and reconciles with Nell. When Nell falls ill from a sprained ankle after walking a roof ridgepole, Thirza realizes how deeply she has come to love her foster daughter. Later, Thirza goes to Port Marlow to hear the Canadian Premier speak, leaving Nell and Obed at home. After Obed dies suddenly from a heart attack caused by the failure of the Abbey Bank, Thirza faces the loss of their life savings and contemplates selling Grey Shutters, but Nell refuses to let the home go and chooses to stay and teach at the Brierley school instead of attending college. Thirza's eyesight deteriorates, requiring a doctor's order to stop reading and sewing, prompting her to invite the widowed Agatha Sowerby to live with her at Grey Shutters so Nell can finally attend Wexcombe College. Years later, Thirza witnesses Nell's graduation with High Honors and her marriage to Hugh Carrow in the orchard of Grey Shutters.

value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the school trustees as the new female teacher for Brierley school. Upon taking up her post in the autumn, she introduced innovative teaching methods, including bi-weekly recitation afternoons, field days in the woods to study nature, and daily physical culture exercises. She formed an advanced Regent's entrance class for dedicated students to provide extra instruction after school hours. During the term, she proposed organizing a Christmas Night concert to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Though she considered a job offer in her home district, she decided to return to Brierley school to guide her students through their final entrance examination year.
